comments.author: @lifeonearth68
comments.text: The part that stuck with me is how ordinary life carries on so close to Mount Pelée—schools, markets, all of it. After what happened in Saint-Pierre, I can’t imagine ever completely forgetting what’s up there. Do people who live nearby talk about the volcano much, or does it become part of the background?

replies.author: @LifewaysTravel
replies.text: It’s fascinating how life continues; while the volcano is a constant presence, for many residents, it’s become a part of the everyday background of island life rather than a daily topic of conversation. 🌋🙏

comments.text: Walking past schools in Saint-Pierre knowing 28,000 people were wiped out in minutes by that volcano is chilling. Living under a mountain that's currently on yellow alert takes an insane amount of mental strength.

comments.author: @HiddenUnrealPlanet
comments.text: Saint-Pierre is a truly spectacular example of a rebirth from the ashes. Passing by the foot of Mount Pelée, I saw it shrouded in mist—at once beautiful and chilling. The locals here must have nerves of steel to live such a laid-back life right beneath a ticking time bomb!

comments.author: @AmazingDiscoveriesTopUS
comments.text: Even so, family ties culture land and homeland keep people on the island, and many who leave return so Martinique is more than a beautiful beach.
